newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open firmer.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open firmer.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open slightly higher Wednesday, as the dollar slipped against the yen overnight and physical demand continued to underpin the bullion market, traders said.
COMEX August gold was seen opening unchanged to up 50 cents an ounce from Tuesday's close at $339.50, after trading between $339.10 and $340.30 in overnight ACCESS trade.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $338.60/00 early, compared to the London Wednesday morning fix at $338.70 an ounce, and the New York close Tuesday around $337.50/00.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks were unchanged at $841,145 ounces Tuesday, while COMEX silver stocks were up 525,162 ounces.
COMEX July silver was seen opening unchanged to up 0.50 cent from the previous close at $4.750 an ounce, after trading between $4.745 and $4.760 in ACCESS.

NYMEX July platinum was seen opening unchanged to up $1.00 an ounce from Tuesday's close at $409.40, while NYMEX September palladium was expected to be unchanged to down $1.00 from the previous close at $178.90.
Russian PGM exports are still expected to resume in late June or early July, but Japanese traders have so far reported no sign of impending deliveries, analysts said.
